1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).
9	
10	One Git submodule:
11	- `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
12	  contract under `include/hybrid/`, pinned by andesim AND by the external vsim, so
13	  there is one source of truth.
14	
15	QEMU and vsim are NOT submodules -- both are prebuilt external binaries:
16	- QEMU: point `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your `qemu-system-*` build dir.
17	- vsim: point `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your external vsim `build/` dir (the
18	  `sim_*` binaries). The vsim sources -- including the vsim-side hybrid
19	  orchestration (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`), `CMakeLists.txt`, and `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`
20	  referenced throughout this doc -- live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo and are
21	  built there (its own `build_vsim.sh`), no longer nested under `verilator/` here.
22	
23	## Build Commands
24	
25	**Primary path (`./andesim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
26	first use), the only driver, used in all user-facing docs.
27	
28	```sh
29	bash scripts/build_all.sh        # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
30	bash scripts/test_all.sh         # unit + contract + e2e suite
31	./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] <elf>
32	./andesim profile [--engine ID] <elf>   # hot-loop detector (engine-synced QEMU; docs/profile.md)
33	./andesim list <models|engines>
34	```
35	
36	**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
37	working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:
38	
39	```sh
40	# Build everything (locate external qemu -> vsim -> plugin)
41	source ./setup.sh
42

44	# config.env's QEMU_BIN_DIR at your qemu-system-* build dir and VSIM_BIN_DIR at

68	and pins the shared ABI as a nested submodule at `external/andesim_abi`.

70	## Running Tests
71	
72	```sh
73	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
74	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
75	
76	# Run with specific options
77	JOBS=4 MODE=marker bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, marker-mode only
78	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)

86	```
87	
88	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
89	
90	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
91	
92	**Manual driver tests**: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` cover the C++ driver's feature contracts. They run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).
93	
94	## Architecture
95	
96	### Two-Phase Handoff
97	
98	```
99	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
100	```
101	
102	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
103	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
104	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands, one write per register. Every CSR write -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block -- also goes through Abstract Commands only, one write per CSR; there is no batched Program-Buffer sweep anywhere in the register/CSR transport, in either direction (a WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch can't be tolerated the way the abstract path's per-CSR cmderr-clear can). `StateDrain` mirrors this: one abstract read per GPR/FPR/CSR. The Program Buffer carries only state the abstract command space cannot reach: the V-data sweep, `vtype`+`vl` (Tier B, see V-State Transport below), and the L2C MMIO window. **Liveness gate**: restores whose drained value equals the engine's own reset value are skipped (a no-op write; each DM op costs ~200-900 simulated cycles). The reset baseline is drained once per (engine build, ELF) on the first hybrid run and cached under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`; `--no-reset-baseline` disables. Never gated: mstatus, GPRs, dpc, dcsr, mcycle, minstret, the S/U PMP mirror. Verify-transparent by construction (skip only when the value is already there).
105	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
106	
107	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The S/U trap CSRs `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are drained by the plugin since v1 and, since the ax66 registration (option A), restored + re-read + `--verify`-compared on S-mode-capable engines (caps gate SMODE; the describe list names them); on an M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) they stay drain-record-only. Other S-mode CSRs (`sstatus`, `sepc`, ...) remain deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
108	
109	**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).
110	
111	### Trigger Modes
112	
113	The repo ships 2 switching modes (triggers); each measures one region you
114	choose. The C++ `andesim` driver exposes them via `--trigger marker|pc`.
115	
116	- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
117	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
118	
119	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. The run yields a cycle figure: window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`).
120	
121	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
122	
123	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`, (v4) the writable M-mode CSR block `struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext`, and (v5) the L2C MMIO register window `struct hybrid_l2c l2c`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
124	
125	**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.
126	
127	**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.
128	
129	**v6 write-mask**: `write_mask[2]` (one bit per mask-governed config CSR, slot map + decode helpers in `include/hybrid/write_mask.h`, live under `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) records **which CSRs the guest actually WROTE** during the QEMU phase. The plugin decodes CSR-write instructions at translation time (`csrrw`/`csrrwi` always write; `csrrs/c` only when rs1!=x0; `csrrsi/ci` only when uimm!=0) and registers an exec callback only on instructions that write a mask-governed CSR -- steady-state code carries zero instrumentation, so the fast leg is unaffected. Consumers (`ResumeDriver` restore, `state_diff` verify) skip any governed CSR whose bit is clear: an untouched CSR's drained value is only QEMU's reset default, which can legitimately differ from the engine's RTL reset value (`msp_bound` all-ones vs 0, `milmb.IEN` 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at ITS OWN reset value -- what real silicon of that engine would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless by construction for every current and future engine, with no per-engine data in QEMU. Governed set: the v3 Andes scalars + PMA, the v4 M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`. Never governed: GPRs/FPRs/V, mstatus, dpc/dcsr, counters, fcsr, the trap-writable CSRs (mepc/mcause/mtval/mip/mie -- hardware writes them without a CSR insn), mtvec/mscratch, and PMP (the S/U mirror is a correctness requirement). `ucode` is transport-always (DSP ops set its sticky OV flag without a CSR insn). Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). 135	### V-State Transport
136	
137	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
138	L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =

152	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).
153	
154	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m8 (vl=8*vlenb), which also forces vstart=0;
155	with LMUL=8 one `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` moves a group of 8 registers, so all 32 move in
156	4 grouped ops in a single Program-Buffer execution. The scratch is packed at the
157	RUNTIME vlenb stride (`stage_v_to_scratch` drops the wire-format
158	`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` padding so each 8-register group is contiguous).
159

161	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS

171	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
172	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
173	
174	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
175	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
176	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.

1	# HTIF Syscall Window Roadmap: uncached mailbox, coherence by construction
2	
3	Goal: `demo/syscall` (and all HTIF file io) passes on EVERY vsim engine,
4	including `vsim:ax66_makatau`, by removing the root cause found on
5	2026-07-14: the host services syscalls by backdoor-writing the flat RAM
6	model, which is invisible through a private write-back L2 (ax66's PL2C).
7	See memory note `ax66-makatau-syscall-bug` for the full evidence chain.
8	
9	Fix: move the syscall mailbox OUT of cacheable RAM into a scratch window
10	inside the SimControl device region. Device space is uncached on every
11	engine (PMA device attribute - empirically proven by UART + doorbell
12	behavior on all 3 engines), so no cache can ever hold a stale copy, in
13	either direction. `flush_dcache()` becomes dead code and is deleted.
14	
15	## The window contract (shared by vsim, QEMU, runtime)
16	
17	- Region: SimControl `0xe0080000 - 0xe0080fff` (existing 4KB on both hosts).
18	- Window: offset `0x800..0xfff` (2KB), device-backed storage:
19	  - `0x800..0x83f`: eight u64 slots - syscall nr/args in, result in slot 0
20	    (same layout as the old RAM magicmem).
21	  - `0x840..0xfff`: 1984-byte data area for payload marshaling.
22	- Doorbell: offset `0x28` (`SYSCALL_GO`), u32/u64 write of any value ->

2	
3	Goal: a prebuilt RISC-V **static glibc** binary (built with the Andes
4	`nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d` toolchain) runs on every andesim mode
5	(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid

65	## Guest memory map (vlinux contract, DRAM base 0x0)
66	
67	| Region                  | Range                          | Owner |
68	|-------------------------|--------------------------------|-------|
69	| ILM aperture            | 0x0000_0000 .. 0x0000_FFFF     | platform (apps link at >= 0x10000, no overlap) |
70	| App image (PT_LOADs)    | link base (0x10000/0x50000) .. | app ELF; loader rejects overlap with vlinux |
71	| brk arena               | app image end .. 0x0200_0000   | `brk` grows up; when full glibc malloc falls back to mmap |

73	| mmap arena              | 0x0220_0000 .. initial stack   | grows DOWN from just below the app stack |
74	| App initial stack       | top 8 MB below `mem_size`      | built by loader (argc/argv/envp/auxv) |
75	| V-scratch               | `mem_size` .. +4 KB            | hybrid V transport (existing, untouched) |
76	
77	DLM aperture 0x200000..0x207fff sits inside the app-image range; content
78	across it is transported by the existing LM sidecars (probe-verified).
79	Every arena bound is checked: exhaustion returns -ENOMEM / fails loudly

139	## 4. Prepare your own program
140	
141	### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine
142	
143	Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
144	and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:
145	
146	```sh
147	riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
148	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
149	```
150	
151	- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
152	- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
153	  compiling outside the repo.
154	- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
155	  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
156	  semihosting library can leak into the link.
157	- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.
158	
159	For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:
160	
161	```sh
162	riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
163	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
164	```
165	
166	C++ works through the same two flags -- just switch the driver to `g++`:
167	
168	```sh
169	riscv64-unknown-elf-g++ -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
170	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.cpp -o your_prog.elf
171	```
172	
173	- Static constructors run before `main` (crt0 walks `.init_array` via
174	  newlib's `__libc_init_array`), and returning from `main` has C++
175	  `exit(rc)` semantics: atexit handlers and static destructors run.
176	- libstdc++ heap containers (`std::string`, `std::vector`, ...) sit on
177	  the runtime heap; the g++ driver adds `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, and the
178	  specs add `crtbegin/crtend`.
179	- Prefer `printf` over `<iostream>`: iostreams add hundreds of KB of
180	  code and static-init work that noticeably lengthens a cycle-mode boot.
181	
182	Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:
183	
184	```sh
185	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
186	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
187	  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
188	```
189	
190	(For C++, add `crtbegin.o`/`crtend.o` around your objects and `-lstdc++
191	-lm` before the group -- or just use the `g++` driver form above.)
192	
193	What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:
194	
195	| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
196	|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
197	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
198	| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
199	| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |
200	
201	A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
202	to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.
203	
204	### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)
205	
206	For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:
207	
208	```c
209	#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */
210	
211	andesim_ROI_begin();
212	my_kernel(a, b, c);
213	andesim_ROI_end();
214	```
215	
216	The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
217	binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
218	Ship one binary; measure when you want.
219	
220	> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
221	> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
222	> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
223	> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
224	> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
225	> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
226	> compiler.
227	
228	### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries
229	
230	`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
231	`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
232	the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the profile command:
233	
234	```sh
235	./andesim profile --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
236	```
237	
238	It runs the binary fast (QEMU, configured like your engine) and reports
239	the hottest loops (function, source line, PCs) with a ready `measure:`
240	line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair you can paste straight into the
241	hybrid command. See section 6 and `docs/profile.md` for the full flag
242	reference.

247	
248	Synopsis:
249	
250	```
251	./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
252	```
253

458	### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI
459	
460	Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
461	covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
462	are filtered out. Open the file in
463	[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.
464	
465	```sh
466	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
467	  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
468	  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
469	```
470	
471	Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
472	`riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
473	disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.
474	
475	Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
476	more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
477	an explicit `--pc-end` instead.

480	
481	Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
482	in hybrid mode.
483	
484	**fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:
485	
486	```sh
487	./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
488	# other terminal:
489	gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
490	```
491	
492	**cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
493	port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
494	debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
495	(from your server config), not at 9104:
496	
497	```sh
498	export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
499	./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
500	```
501	
502	`$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
503	**OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
504	where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
505	9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
506	bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
507	use a current OpenOCD.
508	
509	`--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
510	JTAG bitbang port).
511	
512	### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says
513	
514	The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
515	scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
516	Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
517	(`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.

## 0. What "switching mode" means

The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:

```

```

A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
that region cycle-accurately, then drains the final state. You pick
the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not
have to change between modes.

# Hybrid State Transport: CSR Problems and MMIO Problems

## Background (read this first)

A hybrid run uses TWO simulators for ONE program:

```
  QEMU (fast, no timing)          vsim (slow, cycle-accurate)
  boot + setup code       ---->   the measured region (ROI)
                        "handoff"
```

At the handoff we must make vsim's CPU look EXACTLY like QEMU's CPU at
that moment. The copy has two steps:

- **drain**: read all state out of QEMU into a file (`hybrid_state_v1`).
- **restore**: write that file into the vsim hart through the Debug
  Module, then let it run.

Two kinds of state travel, and their problems are different enough to
list separately:

- **CSR**: a register inside the CPU (mstatus, mcache_ctl, ...),
  accessed by the `csrr`/`csrw` instructions.
- **MMIO**: a register inside a device, reached by a memory address
  (the L2 cache controller at 0xE0500000, ...), accessed by ordinary
  load/store instructions.

**(*) One global caveat.** Every vsim-side fix below is committed as
SOURCE, but the prebuilt `sim_*` binaries were built before ABI v5/v6.
----
# ROADMAP: full Andes-V5 CSR transport coverage

**Goal.** For the supported envelope - bare-metal, single-hart, **M-mode or
M+U-mode**, trap-free ROI - verify the hybrid handoff correctly exchanges state
for **every** CSR in `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7`, with a per-section test and a
machine-checked guarantee that nothing is missed.

**Predecessor.** A now-retired Andes-CSR ROADMAP (RESOLVED) added the v3
Andes block - 13 scalar CSRs + PMA - and the capability-gating flywheel. This
ROADMAP reuses that exact pattern (one X-macro list, capability-gated, parity
flywheel) to cover the remaining writable M-mode CSRs across the whole spec.

## The reality (why not "all 232 round-trip")

The spec's Chapter 5 yields **232 CSR rows**. They split three ways (full table:
`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`):

| group | count | what we do |
|-------|-------|------------|
| **carried today** | 41 | already round-trip through `hybrid_state_v1` |
| **ADD** | 49 | writable M-mode plain state -> expand transport (this ROADMAP) |
| **correctly excluded** | 142 | read-only config (29), RV32 shadows (21), side-effecting (11), N-ext (8), indirect-access (7), debug-internal (6), S/H mode-unsupported (57), other (3) |

"Exchange state" only has meaning for **writable plain architectural state**. A
read-only config register (`mvendorid`, `mmsc_cfg`) has nothing to exchange - each
----
# ROADMAP: engine registration = complete CSR-test gate

Goal (user): `andesim` registers a vsim engine, and registration PASSES only
after every CSR the engine's config supports is completely tested.

## Design principle: measure, don't model

The engine is the ground truth for itself. We stop GUESSING which CSRs exist
from config knobs or spec conditions -- that mapping lives only in the RTL and
is fragile to hand-copy -- and instead ASK the vsim engine directly (a probe).
Each source shrinks to its true minimal job:

| source | role |
|---|---|
| **vsim probe** | THE truth: existent CSR set + reset values (measured on the reset hart) |
| config.inc | identity only: `sha256` = registration key; + fallback for the un-probeable few |
| spec inventory | the map: which addresses to probe, names, DS order, read-side-effect skip-list |
| RTL `existent_csr` | optional cross-check for the read-side-effect CSRs the probe must skip |
| QEMU | workload payload + independent `--verify` oracle -- NOT existence |
